title: Lo Specchio Infernale (ballet)
doubts: Unidentified Italian-titled ballet; nothing found online. The old stub calls it a play at the French Theater; Marie calls it a ballet (014.0185). Stub entry.

title: Le Réveillon
doubts: Identification rests on title, date and Ravel (Palais-Royal actor); Nice theatre not named. Image: Edmond Morin watercolour 1872 (BnF via Commons). Premiere 10 Sept 1872 per Wikipedia 'Henri Meilhac'. 051.0463 and 014.0284 'réveillon' are suppers, not the play. Inventory ids 015.0224/0225 are current.

title: Les Domestiques
doubts: Probable (not certain) identification with Grangé and Deslandes, Variétés 18 June 1861, comédie en trois actes mêlée de chant. 007.0335 is not the play (waiters at the Russian restaurant, Vienna); only 002.0064 is a mention; other 'les domestiques' occurrences are servants.

title: Le Martyre / Le Martyr
doubts: UNRESOLVED. Play/opera seen at Nice by Bête with Hamilton, 'Joanita' mocked. Candidates checked, none shown: d'Ennery and Brésil Le Martyr, Donizetti Les Martyrs, Duprez opera Joanita (1852). Stub entry, identification open.

title: Les Pattes de mouche
doubts: Inventory ids 022.0418/0447 are stale (post-rebuild renumbering); real mentions are 022.0429 and 022.0458 (Spa, 6-7 Aug 1874). 013.0130 'pattes de mouche' is the idiom for scrawl. Image is a cropped BnF press engraving, 1860.

title: Much Ado about Nothing / Shakespeare comedy
doubts: 034.0406 and 067.0374 use the title as a proverbial phrase (English); neither proves she read the play. 086.0762 (21 Dec 1879) clearly describes Beatrice and Benedick but does not name the play; 059.0686 'une comédie de Shakespeare' is unnamed and may be another play. A Dicksee 'Beatrice' painting was considered and dropped (no proof it depicts the Much Ado character). Inventory ids current.
